result.markdown: --- title: "Probability and stochastic processes" course-unit: p02-probability-and-stochastic-processes status: complete --- ## Why this unit matters - Epidemics in finite populations are **random**: whether a contact transmits, or an individual recovers today, are chance events. - We build the probability the course needs — Bernoulli/Binomial, mean and variance, the **Markov property** — and apply it to a stochastic SIR chain. - Deterministic ODEs describe the *mean*; here we capture the *fluctuations*. ## Equations {.smaller} A sum of $n$ independent Bernoulli$(p)$ trials is Binomial$(n,p)$: $$ \Pr(X=k)=\binom{n}{k}p^k(1-p)^{n-k},\quad \mathbb{E}[X]=np,\quad \operatorname{Var}[X]=np(1-p). $$ {#eq-s-p02-binom} Per-step probabilities from the SIR rates, then a Markov update: $$ p_I = 1-e^{-\beta c I_t \delta t/N},\quad p_R = 1-e^{-\gamma\delta t}, $$ {#eq-s-p02-probs} $$ Y_t\sim\text{Bin}(S_t,p_I),\; Z_t\sim\text{Bin}(I_t,p_R),\; S_{t+1}=S_t-Y_t,\; I_{t+1}=I_t+Y_t-Z_t,\; R_{t+1}=R_t+Z_t. $$ {#eq-s-p02-chain} Only current counts enter — the **Markov property** — and $N$ is conserved. ## Julia API: the Markov kernel ::: {#cell-s-p02-kernel .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} using Distributions, StableRNGs rate_to_proportion(r, δt) = -expm1(-r * δt) function chain_step(state, p, δt, rng) S, I, R = state; β, c, γ, N = p Y = rand(rng, Binomial(S, rate_to_proportion(β * c * I / N, δt))) # infections Z = rand(rng, Binomial(I, rate_to_proportion(γ, δt))) # recoveries return (S - Y, I + Y - Z, R + Z) end function simulate(u0, p, δt, nsteps, rng) traj = Matrix{Int}(undef, 3, nsteps + 1); traj[:, 1] .= u0 s = Tuple(u0) for k in 1:nsteps; s = chain_step(s, p, δt, rng); traj[:, k+1] .= s; end traj end ``` ::: {#s-p02-kernel .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` simulate (generic function with 1 method) ``` ::: ::: ## Generated result: an ensemble ::: {#cell-fig-s-p02-ensemble .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} using CairoMakie u0 = [990, 10, 0]; p = (0.05, 10.0, 0.25, 1000); δt = 1.0; nsteps = 40; nsims = 200 ens = [simulate(u0, p, δt, nsteps, StableRNG(seed)) for seed in 1:nsims] Ipaths = reduce(hcat, (t[2, :] for t in ens)); meanI = vec(sum(Ipaths; dims = 2)) ./ nsims ts = 0:nsteps fig = Figure(size = (760, 380)); ax = Axis(fig[1,1]; xlabel = "day", ylabel = "I(t)") for j in 1:nsims; lines!(ax, ts, Ipaths[:, j]; color = (:grey, 0.12)); end lines!(ax, ts, meanI; color = :firebrick, linewidth = 3, label = "ensemble mean") axislegend(ax; position = :rt); fig ``` ::: {#fig-s-p02-ensemble .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html} ``` Two hundred stochastic realisations of $I(t)$ (grey) with the ensemble mean (red). Individual epidemics fluctuate and some fade early; the mean is smooth and reproducible. ::: ::: ## Validation Sample mean of a Binomial draw → $np$; every realisation conserves $N$: ::: {#cell-s-p02-check .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} rng = StableRNG(7); n, prob = 990, 0.02 samples = [rand(rng, Binomial(n, prob)) for _ in 1:100_000] mean_ok = isapprox(sum(samples) / length(samples), n * prob; rtol = 0.02) cons_ok = all(t -> all(k -> sum(t[:, k]) == 1000, 1:nsteps+1), ens) (mean_ok, cons_ok) ``` ::: {#s-p02-check .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (true, true) ``` ::: ::: Both `true`: the empirical mean matches $np$ and all $200\times41$ totals equal $N$. ## Limitations & takeaways - The binomial chain captures **demographic stochasticity** the ODE ignores. - It is exact only as $\delta t\to0$: infections and recoveries within a step are treated in separate binomials and assumed independent. - Event-by-event exactness → the **Gillespie** algorithm (jump-process chapter). - **Takeaways:** Binomial = sum of Bernoullis; convert rates to per-step probabilities; seed local RNGs; average an ensemble to recover the mean. ::: {.notes} Explain why variance peaks near p = 0.5 from the np(1-p) formula, and why finer steps reduce the within-step double-event artefact. Note that the ensemble mean approaches the deterministic solution studied in the Foundations chapter, which motivates the map-versus-chain comparison in Discrete-time models. Encourage learners to open the notebook and vary the seed range and step width. ::: ## Learn more - Book chapter: [Probability and stochastic processes](../../prerequisites/02-probability-and-stochastic-processes.html) - Pluto notebook: [`02-probability-and-stochastic-processes.jl`](../../notebooks/prerequisites/02-probability-and-stochastic-processes.jl) - [Distributions.jl](https://juliastats.org/Distributions.jl/stable/)
